location: cell-contract.md > Plan > Run scope + Phase 1; tier-matrix.md Rules (Tier 0 runs inside the Phase 1 loop of ... the focus cell's version)
issue: The plan's `--versions` carries two meanings in the same call. Phase 1 calls the plan with `--versions V --per-version`, and `phase1_reuse` is computed for that V. The same `--versions` is also the run scope that filters `e2e_next_cells`. After a loop-back with focus (8.1, firefox), the hosting loop is 8.1's. When the derivation reaches `cold-canary`, the only next cell is 9.1:chromium, the `--versions 8.1` filter removes it, and `e2e_step` becomes `blocked-by-scope`. That ends the E2E loop (cell-contract > Plan, last bullet) instead of running the canary. The same thing happens in any non-canary hosting loop that derives `gate`.
implementation_impact: Following the text literally makes every loop-back dead-end at step 3 (cold canary). I cannot tell whether the hosting loop must call the plan twice (once with `--versions V` for `phase1_reuse`, once with the operator's run scope for E2E) or whether the scope filter is skipped for loop-back steps.
suggestion: State explicitly that the E2E step in the hosting loop comes from a plan call whose `--versions`/`--browsers` are the operator's run scope (default: all configured), separate from the `--versions V` call that yields `phase1_reuse`. Or add a separate flag (e.g. `--phase1-version V`) so the two meanings never share one argument. Add a test: a loop-back hosted in 8.1 derives `cold-canary` with `e2e_next_cells` = [9.1:chromium], not `blocked-by-scope`.

location: cell-contract.md > State, freshness, gate-grade (Passing gate-grade) + Plan steps 2/4/5; tier-matrix.md Rules (inconclusive cell blocks promotion: ... rerun that cell)
issue: Some cells pass but can never become passing gate-grade on unchanged source: a smoke-only module (`authored_assertions` = 0), any skipped spec (`scenario_notes` non-empty, including a git-deleted spec), a persistent `browser_notes`, BO steps that are always inconclusive, or a deterministic infra cause such as a missing image when pull is not allowed. For such a canary the derivation repeats `cold-canary` (fresh pass, lacks PGG) or `focus` forever. `gate` is never reached, the hosting Phase 1 loop (which ends only at `gate`/`done`) never ends, and Phase 2 never starts. The only exits defined are E2E `skipped` and `blocked-by-scope`.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator loops on identical cold boots with no stop condition. I would have to invent a terminal state, a retry cap, or a rule to proceed to Phase 2 with `ready=false`.
suggestion: Add a terminal step (e.g. `e2e_step: blocked-not-gradeable`, listing the cells and the reason: smoke-only, scenario_notes, browser_notes, inconclusive steps, missing field). The plan emits it when the newest cold full record is fresh, conclusive `pass`, and still not PGG. Treat it like `skipped` and `blocked-by-scope`: it ends the E2E loop and Phase 2 runs its other layers. For repeated inconclusive infra causes, define a retry limit (e.g. same fingerprint + same reason twice), after which the step is reported as blocked rather than rerun.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1 (hosting loop ends only when ... `e2e_step` is `gate` or `done`) and last bullet; SKILL.md Lapis 4 (`psm_e2e_enabled` is an orchestrator gate)
issue: Nothing says how the hosting loop or Phase 2 behaves when `psm_e2e_enabled` is false, or when the operator gates without E2E (`ps-aggregate.py --require` without `e2e`, which cell-contract > Configured cells keeps allowed). The plan still derives `focus`/`gate` steps, and the canary loop waits for `gate`/`done`, which never arrive because E2E never runs.
implementation_impact: For modules or runs with E2E disabled, the Phase 1 loop of the canary version never terminates. I would have to guess whether the plan suppresses the E2E fields or the orchestrator ignores them.
suggestion: Add a rule: with `psm_e2e_enabled` false (or E2E not in the required layers), the plan emits `e2e_step: disabled` (or the orchestrator treats it like `skipped`), the hosting loop ignores the E2E condition, and Phase 2 runs no tier 1.

location: SPEC.md CAP-1 intent ('Phase 2 starts only after every version is clean on Layers 1, 2, and 5'); tier-matrix.md tier 1 'Starts when'; cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1 ('Phase 2 starts when every version's loop has ended')
issue: Two conditions for starting Phase 2 disagree, and the plan computes neither. 'Every version clean on Layers 1/2/5' is a current-freshness condition. 'Every version's loop has ended' is historical. A patch made in a later version's loop (or in the canary loop, or during a loop-back) stales Layers 1/2/5 of versions whose loops already ended. Whether those loops must reopen before tier 1 is not stated. The plan's `gate` step checks only canary PGG and failing cells, never Layers 1/2/5 of the other versions, yet the orchestrator is told to run exactly `e2e_next_cells` and 'never pick a tier by judgment'. Also unspecified: the order of the version loops (canary first or last), and the order of Layer 1/2/5 work versus the tier-0 E2E run inside the canary loop.
implementation_impact: I cannot implement the Phase 1 → Phase 2 transition deterministically. I would have to choose whether the orchestrator holds back a plan-emitted `gate` until other versions converge (judgment the contract forbids), and whether each loop-back patch reopens all three Phase 1 loops (three more flashlight/scenario boot rounds).
suggestion: Make the plan own the condition. For example, `gate` is emitted only when `phase1_reuse` holds for every configured version (otherwise a new step such as `wait-phase1` with the versions still dirty). State the loop order (e.g. canary version first, so its patches happen before the other versions converge) and say explicitly that a patch reopens every version whose Layers 1/2/5 became stale.

location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Owner ('writes `session.json` in its registry dir (`<tmp>/psm-jobs/<warm-id>/`)') and Attach (lease file); ps-flashlight-run.py `_registry_entries`, `_job_unregister`, `stop_job`
issue: The job registry treats every `*.json` in `<tmp>/psm-jobs/<job>/` as a process entry (`_registry_entries` globs `*.json`). `session.json` has no `host`/`pid`, so `entry_state` reports it as `foreign`, and `--list-jobs`/`--stop-job` show it as a bogus process. `_job_unregister` and `stop_job` remove the directory only when it is empty (`rmdir`), so `session.json` and `lease` keep a dead keeper's directory alive. `--use-warm auto` then finds a stale `session.json` by module path and version.
implementation_impact: Implemented as written, this breaks `--list-jobs` output and leaves stale warm-session records that `auto` can pick up.
suggestion: Put the session file under a non-`.json` name or a subdirectory (e.g. `warm/session.json`). Make `_registry_entries` read only `<pid>.json`. Make the keeper and `stop_job` delete `session.json` and `lease` on teardown. Make `auto` verify that the keeper PID in the session file is alive (`entry_state`) before attaching.

location: cell-contract.md > Warm container (Owner, Attach, Teardown); SPEC.md CAP-5
issue: The warm invocation chain is not specified. (a) Who launches `ps-e2e-run.py --keep-warm`: the orchestrator directly, ps-run-layer, or the iteration process? (b) Does the iteration that starts the keeper also drive the browsers through it, or does the keeper only boot? (c) How do `--keep-warm`/`--use-warm` reach the child through `ps-run-layer --cells`: passthrough after `--`, or new ps-run-layer flags? (d) Who performs the teardowns listed under Teardown ('before a cold run', 'when the focus cell changes', 'when the loop ends') and how they find the warm Job ID. (e) What flag carries `psm_e2e_warm_ttl` to the keeper. (f) How the keeper's in-process boot timings reach the iteration's record (`boot_phases` with the keeper's `boot_id`).
implementation_impact: Every one of these is a guess. Different guesses produce incompatible CLIs and change which process owns the container. That matters for `--cleanup-orphans` (owner-pid) and for the CAP-5 assertion 'no bring-up in the iteration's own progress log'.
suggestion: Add a short sequence: orchestrator → `ps-run-layer --cells V:b --warm` → the child runs `--use-warm auto`; if no keeper exists, it spawns a detached `--keep-warm --warm-ttl N`, waits for `session.json`, and then attaches. ps-run-layer (not the orchestrator) stops any live keeper for the module via `--stop-job` before a cold step, and the orchestrator stops it when the loop ends. The keeper copies its `boot_phases` into `session.json` for the iteration to embed.

location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > `psm_e2e_slots` (host-wide count via `<tmp>/psm-jobs/`, 'each live E2E job records the slots it holds'); SPEC.md Constraints (shared WSL Docker daemon)
issue: Slot accounting is underspecified. (1) The registry stores one `<pid>.json` per process. Whether slots are recorded per PID, per job, or per container is undefined, and so is how CAP-7 workers, the version process and a keeper avoid double counting. (2) There is no atomic admission, so two sessions can read the same free count and both admit; no lock is specified. (3) The registry lives in `tempfile.gettempdir()`. Sessions with different `TMPDIR`, or several WSL distros sharing one Docker Desktop daemon (the stated reason for the cap), do not see each other's entries, so the 'host-wide' cap is not host-wide. (4) The `wait-slots` heartbeat lines are written before the child starts, and the child's `progress_init` truncates that same log. (5) Who decides that the second engine has no slot (sequential fallback): ps-run-layer or the version process? How does the child learn how many slots it holds? (6) Whether `wait-slots` is a CAP-6 phase, and in which field.
implementation_impact: I would have to design the slot schema, the locking, and the fallback handshake myself. Races and the per-TMPDIR blind spot would silently break the stated purpose (avoiding `wait-healthy` stalls).
suggestion: Specify: a registry field `slots` on the entry of the process that owns the container (the keeper for a warm job), a host-level `flock` on `<registry>/slots.lock` around count-and-register, a fixed registry path that does not depend on TMPDIR (or counting via Docker labels such as `psm.slots` so every daemon client sees it), a `--slots-granted N` from ps-run-layer to the child, and the log/timing placement of `wait-slots`.

location: cell-contract.md > Runner (Fail-fast) and Parallel browsers ('When the cap leaves no room for the second engine, the version drives its browsers sequentially'); SPEC.md Assumptions (fail-fast stops only unstarted cells)
issue: Fail-fast is defined at ps-run-layer level ('first child that exits 3 ... starts no further queued cell'), but a child can hold an unstarted cell of its own: the second engine in the sequential fallback. If the first engine fails conclusively, the text does not say whether the child still runs the second engine (it is unstarted, so fail-fast says stop) or reports it `not-run`. The child cannot see ps-run-layer's decision. ps-run-layer's own exit code after a fail-fast stop, `not-run` or `no-slots` cells is also not given (it is only told to treat a child's 3 like 1).
implementation_impact: The CAP-3 behaviour differs depending on slot pressure, and orchestrator scripts that branch on ps-run-layer's exit code have no contract.
suggestion: Specify that in the sequential fallback the version process applies fail-fast itself: after a conclusive fail on the first engine, the second engine gets a `not-run` record (`reason: fail-fast after V:b`). Give ps-run-layer's exit codes for e2e (e.g. 3 when any cell failed, 1 when only infra/not-run/no-slots, 0 when all driven cells pass).

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Fields (`started_at`/`finished_at` = 'this cell's engine start and end', `run_id`, `tier`, `boot_id`) and Newest/latest
issue: Several required fields have no defined source. (a) `not-run` and `no-slots` cells, and cells whose boot or install failed before any engine started, have no engine start or end. Yet 'newest' is ordered by `started_at`, the plan must report `not-run` 'when it is the cell's newest record', and 'a record with a missing field is never gate-grade'. (b) `run_id`: `RUN_ID` is per process, so each child and each CAP-7 `--engine-worker` has a different one. Which one goes in the record? (c) `tier`: ps-run-layer has no input that tells it the tier. (d) `boot_id` format and its value for warm iterations (keeper boot or iteration).
implementation_impact: Each implementer will pick different values. That changes the ordering of 'newest', which drives `failing`, `recorded failure`, `focus` and the `not-run` reason.
suggestion: Define: `started_at` = the time the cell was admitted or the stop was decided, for cells that never drove (and `finished_at` = same); `run_id` = the version process's RUN_ID; a new `ps-run-layer --tier N` (or derive tier from the plan output passed in); `boot_id` = the RUN_ID of the process that ran bring-up (the keeper's for warm).

location: cell-contract.md > Plan ('Focus cell = the failing cell from the newest run (ties: `psm_target_versions` order, then `psm_e2e_browsers` order)')
issue: 'Run' is undefined. Records carry per-cell `started_at`, a per-process `run_id`, a per-invocation `job_id` and a per-boot `boot_id`. If the newest run means the newest record's `started_at`, the two cells of a parallel CAP-7 pair that both fail differ by milliseconds, so the tie rule never fires and the focus cell depends on scheduling. That contradicts the deterministic choice used for the `not-run` reason ('first in `psm_e2e_browsers` order'). The text also does not say whether 'psm_target_versions order' means config order or the normalizer's numeric order.
implementation_impact: The focus cell, and therefore which warm container and which loop-back version are used, is non-deterministic, and a unit test of the tie rule cannot be written.
suggestion: Define the newest run as the max `job_id` start (or ps-run-layer invocation) among failing cells' newest cold full records. Then apply the tie order across all failing cells of that invocation, using the normalized numeric version order.

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record (per-cell `browser_notes`, 'Fields that live at version level today (errors, install, scenario_notes) are copied into every cell'); ps-e2e-run.py run_one_version (`probe_missed`, `browser_notes`)
issue: Today `browser_notes` is a version-level list of free-text strings, and it includes notes about other engines, e.g. 'engine tak dijalankan (binary belum di-playwright install): firefox'. Passing gate-grade requires `browser_notes` empty per cell, but nothing says how notes are attributed to an engine. Copied wholesale, a missing firefox binary makes the chromium cell non-PGG. Also, a requested engine that the binary probe dropped never 'drove', and ps-run-layer appends records only 'for each cell the run drove', so that cell gets no record and the cause is invisible to plan and aggregate. Separately, brownfield/cell-contract call `scenario_notes` version-level, but today it is a top-level run field in ps-e2e-run.py `main`.
implementation_impact: Copying version-level notes falsely blocks a healthy cell. Filtering them requires parsing strings. A probe-missed cell silently keeps reason `missing` or an old record.
suggestion: Make the runner emit `browser_notes` keyed by engine (structured). Write a record with `state: inconclusive, reason: browser-unavailable` for every requested-but-undriven engine. Correct the source of `scenario_notes` (run-level, copied into each cell).

location: cell-contract.md > Plan (`rerun_matrix` reasons: missing, stale-source, stale-tag, warm-only, partial, inconclusive, not-run; `e2e_tier`)
issue: The reason enum has no value for (a) a cell whose newest cold full fresh record is `fail`, or (b) a fresh, cold, full, conclusive `pass` that is not passing gate-grade (`authored_assertions` 0, non-empty `scenario_notes`/`browser_notes`/`inconclusive`, missing field). No precedence is given when several reasons apply (e.g. stale-source and partial). `e2e_tier` has no value for `done`.
implementation_impact: I must invent reason strings and an ordering. Tests and the headless `versions[ver].reason` will then disagree with whatever the doc author intended.
suggestion: Add `fail` and `not-gate-grade:<cause>` to the enum. Give a precedence (e.g. missing > stale-tag > stale-source > fail > not-run > inconclusive > warm-only > partial > not-gate-grade). Set `e2e_tier` to null (or 1) for `done`.

location: cell-contract.md > Aggregate ('Every other E2E field it emits is derived from the records it selected'); ps-aggregate.py e2e_layer/merge_version/main; references/e2e-quickstart.md line 82
issue: The selection rule is given only for `ready` (passing gate-grade per cell). It is not given for `pass` and E2E `findings` (does a stale `fail`, or a fresh warm/partial `fail`, block `pass`?), for the per-version `versions[ver].layers.e2e` state, `conclusive`, `inconclusive_note` and `versions[ver].ready`, or for `e2e_conclusive`, `e2e_smoke_only`, `e2e_scenario_notes` and `e2e_screenshot_dir`. It is also not given for `e2e_cells.state` when the newest record is `not-run` but 'hides no older record'. Explicit-file mode (`--e2e file` without `--reports-dir`, documented in e2e-quickstart.md:82) is not addressed now that E2E comes 'only from histories'.
implementation_impact: `pass` is consumed by psm-optimize's 'no new failures' delta and by sibling skills' per-version status. Each guess changes those verdicts.
suggestion: Specify per field which record is used. For example, per cell: the newest fresh conclusive cold full record if any, else the newest record; `pass` is blocked by findings of that record only; the per-version E2E layer is the conjunction over that version's configured cells. Say what `--e2e <file>` does (rejected, or read as a report view without gating) and add e2e-quickstart.md to the docs-to-update list.

location: SPEC.md CAP-6 success + Success signal ('the canary version boots twice ... CAP-6 timings show both'); cell-contract.md > Phase timings (`e2e_phase_durations[ver] = {boot: {...}, browsers: {...}}`, 'counting each `boot_id` once', warm `reset-*` into `boot_phases`)
issue: The aggregate shape holds one `boot` object per version, but the verdict records of the canary version come from at least two boots: the cold canary run (chromium) and the tier 1 boot (firefox), and more after a loop-back. The success signal requires showing both. Warm iterations share the keeper's `boot_id`, yet each has its own `reset-db`/`reset-files`/`reset-opcache` and `install`, which the contract puts in `boot_phases`. 'Count each boot_id once' would collapse different iterations. Repeated per-engine phases (`lock-wait:<engine>` once per BO scenario, and the sequential rerun after a failed BO login producing a second `browser:<engine>`) have no suffix or sum rule; `#2` is defined only for boot phases.
implementation_impact: The CAP-6 output cannot satisfy its own success criterion as specified, and the warm timings would be wrong.
suggestion: Change the shape to `e2e_phase_durations[ver] = {boots: {<boot_id>: {...}}, browsers: {<engine>: {...}}}`. Give warm iterations their own per-iteration id (e.g. `iteration_id`) for reset/install timings. State that repeated cell phases get `#n` suffixes (or are summed, with a count).

location: cell-contract.md > Headless ('returns at the first step that is not clean'); tier-matrix.md Rules ('A tier is clean when ...'); cell-contract.md > Plan step 5 (`e2e_scenarios: failed-only`)
issue: 'Clean' is defined for tiers, not for steps (`focus`, `cold-version`, `cold-canary`). Headless never uses the warm container but is not told to ignore `e2e_scenarios: failed-only`. A headless focus step after a recorded failure therefore runs a cold partial run. Even when it passes, it can never be gate-grade, so the step is never clean: headless returns after a passing run, and the caller needs another invocation to reach `cold-canary`/`gate`.
implementation_impact: I would have to guess the per-step clean test, and whether headless overrides `e2e_scenarios`. The wrong guess roughly doubles headless boots after every fix.
suggestion: Define step clean = every cell in that step's `e2e_next_cells` has passing gate-grade evidence after the run. Specify that headless always runs `full` (the plan emits `failed-only` only when interactive, or headless overrides it), so a passing headless focus run is gate-grade.

location: cell-contract.md > Headless ('Before returning it always runs ps-aggregate.py; when it stops before Phase 2 ...'); ps-aggregate.py main (requires `<module>-static.json`; reads canonical `<module>-<layer>.json`)
issue: Canonical files for Layers 1/2/5 are produced in Phase 2 (run-phases.md: merge-only and the cross-version static run). When headless stops at a tier-0 step during Phase 1, those canonical files may be missing (aggregate exits 2 without `--static`) or stale from a previous session. Aggregate would then report other layers from old evidence. The spec does not say how aggregate gets current Layer 1/2/5 inputs on an early stop.
implementation_impact: The headless return could be `blocked` (exit 2) or carry stale per-version verdicts for layers that were actually re-run per version in Phase 1.
suggestion: Specify that on an early stop, headless first runs `ps-run-layer --merge-only` for Layers 2/5 and the cross-version static scan, or that aggregate gains a per-version input mode. Alternatively, require headless to report `ready:false` with the per-version Phase 1 plan results instead of calling aggregate.

location: cell-contract.md > Configured cells ('only source of the required set ... read directly from the --config JSON'); SPEC.md Constraints (headless callers keep their per-version verdict contract); references/headless.md (versions from arguments); psm-cross-version/psm-develop SKILL.md (take versions from arguments)
issue: Headless callers pass target versions as arguments, and headless.md uses config only 'bila argumen tak menyebutnya' (when the arguments don't name them). Under this contract, caller-supplied versions are only run scope, so a caller validating `--versions 8.1,9.1` with the default 3-version config always gets `ready=false` and `e2e_state: inconclusive` for 1.7.8. Before, it got a verdict for the versions it asked for. That changes the per-version verdict contract the SPEC promises to keep.
implementation_impact: I cannot tell whether headless arguments should feed the configured set (e.g. by writing a derived config) or whether sibling skills' behaviour is meant to change.
suggestion: Decide whether headless explicit versions/browsers define the configured set for that run. If they do, have headless write them into the `--config` JSON it passes on. Either way, update references/headless.md and state that sibling callers are affected.

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage ('Plan and aggregate read E2E evidence only from these histories'), Runner (`--cells`), Docs to update; SKILL.md Lapis 4 (direct `ps-e2e-run.py`); references/e2e-quickstart.md lines 43/72/139/150; references/run-phases.md Fase 2 (`--layer e2e --versions ... --per-version`, `--merge-only`)
issue: It is unclear which E2E entry points write history records. Records are appended by ps-run-layer 'after the child exits', and the text says that only `--cells` writes no per-version file. Unanswered: (a) does `ps-run-layer --layer e2e --versions ... --per-version` (still legal, since `--cells` is only mutually exclusive with `--versions`) also append history, or is it removed for e2e? (b) Do direct `ps-e2e-run.py` runs (SKILL.md Lapis 4 and the quickstart TDD loop) append anything? (c) What inputs does `--merge-only --layer e2e` now take (`--versions`? `--config`?), and is its old mtime=oldest rule kept? (d) After the upgrade, every existing `<module>-e2e-<ver>.json` is ignored, so all cells read `missing`. Is that intended? It is not stated.
implementation_impact: Evidence produced by documented commands could silently not count, or the old per-version path keeps writing files nobody reads.
suggestion: List the supported E2E entry points. Either make every ps-run-layer e2e invocation append history (and reject `--per-version` for e2e), or remove the `--versions` form for e2e. Say that direct ps-e2e-run.py output is never evidence. Define the `--merge-only` inputs for e2e. Add a migration note (old per-version files ignored; first run re-proves everything).

location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Reset per iteration (`reset-opcache`: 'reload PHP-FPM/Apache'; `reset-files`)
issue: The command that reloads the web server inside each flashlight image is not given and not verified. Default tags mix Apache (`1.7.8.11`) and nginx+php-fpm (`8.1.6-nginx`, `9.1.4-nginx`), and the process supervisor inside the images is unknown. If the tested module already exists in the image baseline (a native module name), `reset-files` keeps `modules/<mod>`. INSTALL_BLOCK_SH's `cp -r /ps-module-src modules/$MOD_NAME` then copies into a nested `modules/<mod>/ps-module-src`, and the old code stays installed.
implementation_impact: Implementing `reset-opcache` requires discovering per-image commands. A wrong choice leaves stale opcache, so warm results test old code without any error being raised.
suggestion: Specify the reload command per image family (or verify `kill -USR2` on the php-fpm master and `apachectl graceful`, with a fallback that makes the iteration inconclusive). Make reset-files always remove `modules/<mod>` (or make the copy `rm -rf` the target first). Add a test that checks a changed PHP constant is visible over HTTP in iteration N+1.

location: SPEC.md CAP-7 success + cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers ('Identical findings' on bankwire; lock-wait > startup timeout → inconclusive)
issue: The equality test is not deterministic, given how the existing fixtures share state. FO-only scenarios run without the lock and share one DB with the other engine. bankwire `checkout-empty-banks-safe` (FO-only, assumes zero banks and seeds the cart) can run before, during or after the other engine's `checkout-with-bank` adds 'Bank Niaga E2E', so the interleaving changes from run to run. A long BO scenario (checkout-with-bank waits up to 30 s per `wait_for_text`, and cold 1.7/8 are slow) can push the other engine's `lock-wait` past the 180 s startup timeout. That turns a scenario inconclusive and breaks equality. The test's repetition count and the procedure when the sets differ are not given.
implementation_impact: The done criterion can pass or fail by scheduling luck, so CAP-7 cannot be signed off reliably.
suggestion: Fix the comparison procedure: N runs of each, the sequential reference forced with `--slots 1`, and an allowed-difference rule (or require equality across N=3). Give lock-wait its own timeout (e.g. sum of the holder's scenario budget) rather than the startup timeout. Note the bankwire FO/BO shared-state caveat in the fixture.

location: SPEC.md Success signal ('once the canary has a recorded failure, a fix-loop iteration after a one-line patch completes as a warm canary run with no boot phase')
issue: This conflicts with CAP-5 and CAP-6. The first warm-eligible iteration starts the keeper, and CAP-5 itself says only iterations 'after the one that started the keeper' skip bring-up/wait-healthy. Every warm iteration also runs `install`, which CAP-6 lists among the 'shared boot phases'. Read literally, 'no boot phase' is false for any warm iteration.
implementation_impact: An acceptance check written from the Success signal fails against a correct implementation.
suggestion: Reword it to: 'the second and later warm iterations show no `pull`, `bring-up` or `wait-healthy` phase', matching the CAP-5 success.

location: SPEC.md Why / Open Questions
issue: No done criterion measures the outcome the request is about (cutting 'all day'). The success criteria check behaviour (tiers, warm, timings, parallel overlap) but not elapsed time. The wall-clock budget is explicitly left open.
implementation_impact: The feature can be 'done' without demonstrably shortening a validation. I cannot tell when performance work (slot defaults, parallelism) is sufficient.
suggestion: Add at least a relative criterion. For example, on bankwire, the clean-module end-to-end E2E wall clock (sum of the CAP-6 boot and browser durations) is ≤ X% of the sequential baseline measured with the current scripts, and one warm iteration takes ≤ Y min. Record the baseline as part of the work.

location: SPEC.md frontmatter (`sources: []`) and Assumptions ('The canary defaults to the newest target (9.1) × Chromium ... Budi named "9 + Chrome"')
issue: The originating request (Budi's in-chat message and his answers) is not recorded as a source, so the claims cannot be traced back. Two source claims also changed meaning slightly. 'Version 9' became 'newest configured target', so adding 10.0 (which the normalizer explicitly anticipates) silently moves the canary off version 9. 'Chrome' became Playwright Chromium (not branded Chrome); the spec states this mapping only implicitly.
